question:
A 61-year-old man visits his primary care provider due to recurrent episodes of dizziness and
generalized weakness. His medical history includes hyperlipidemia and atrial fibrillation, for which he is
prescribed atorvastatin and high-dose flecainide as a “pill-in-the-pocket” regimen. He reports taking
flecainide whenever he experiences atrial fibrillation episodes. After evaluation, the physician suspects
that flecainide is the cause of his dizziness. After discussing treatment options, they decide to switch
the flecainide to diltiazem. This decision represents which type of disease prevention? Answer
Choices: (A) Primary (B) Quaternary (C) Preventive pharmacology (D) Clinical prevention (E) Harm
reduction (F) Primordial (G) Therapeutic modification (H) Secondary (I) Risk factor modification (J)
Tertiary
 A. Risk factor modification
B. Quaternary
C. Secondary
D. Therapeutic modification
E. Clinical prevention
F. Primordial
G. Harm reduction
H. Primary
I. Preventive pharmacology
J. Tertiary
